title: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness - Pre Vocational Studies - Fishery
exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Fishery is best defined as the branch of agriculture that deals primarily with the ________.
options: Rearing, catching, and processing of fish and other aquatic organisms
Hunting of wild life in the forest
questions.explain: Fishery involves all activities related to the production, capturing, processing, and management of fish and other commercially valuable aquatic animals.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Fish that spend their entire life cycle in inland waters such as rivers, lakes, streams, and ponds are classified based on their habitat as ________.
questions.explain: Fresh water fish (such as Tilapia and Catfish) naturally inhabit waters with very low or zero salt content, such as lakes, ponds, rivers, and streams.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Which of the following aquatic environments is the natural habitat for salt water fish?
questions.explain: Salt water (marine) fish, such as sharks and mackerels, live in environments with high salinity, predominantly oceans and seas.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Fish species that possess a hard, calcified skeleton instead of cartilage are morphologically classified as ________.
questions.explain: Based on morphology (body structure), fish with skeletons made entirely of hard true bones (e.g., Tilapia, Catfish, Croaker) are known as bony fish.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: A shark is morphologically classified as a cartilaginous fish because its internal skeleton is completely composed of ________.
questions.explain: Cartilaginous fish (like sharks and rays) lack hard, calcified bones; their skeletons are composed entirely of cartilage, which is a tough and flexible tissue.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Which of the following organisms is considered an aquatic agricultural organism but is NOT a true fish?
questions.explain: While shrimps, crabs, and oysters are aquatic organisms harvested and farmed in fisheries, they are technically shellfish (crustaceans and mollusks), not true finfish.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: In the human diet, the primary nutritional use of fish and fish products is to provide a rich supply of ________.
questions.explain: Fish is highly valued globally as food because its flesh provides essential, easily digestible, high-quality animal protein required for human growth and tissue repair.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Which of the following is a vital agricultural product manufactured from the bones and waste of processed fish and used extensively as an ingredient in livestock feeds?
questions.explain: Fish meal is a very valuable by-product produced by grinding fish waste into a powder. It is heavily used in compounding protein-rich feeds for poultry and livestock.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: A common fishing method that involves throwing or dragging a large, woven mesh structure into the water to entangle and trap multiple fish at once is known as ________.
questions.explain: Netting is the use of different types of nets (cast nets, trawlers, gill nets) to capture a large quantity of fish efficiently from the water.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Which basic traditional method of catching fish relies on an attached bait, a sinker, and a sharp metal curve to snare individual fish by the mouth?
questions.explain: Hook and line fishing is a manual method using bait placed on a metal hook. When the fish swallows the bait, it is hooked by the mouth and pulled out.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Releasing untreated industrial effluents directly into rivers creates a serious risk factor in fishery primarily because it ________.
options: Makes the fish grow exceptionally large
Pollutes the water with toxic chemicals that kill the fish
Provides alternative organic food for the fish
questions.explain: Industrial effluents contain heavy metals and toxic chemicals. When released into water bodies, they cause severe water pollution, leading to the mass death of aquatic organisms.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Why is the use of harmful chemicals (such as Gammalin 20) as a method for catching fish strictly prohibited and considered a major risk factor?
options: It causes the fishing nets to tear easily
It contaminates the fish, making them dangerous for human consumption
It forces the fish to migrate to other countries
It makes the water too clear to see the fish
questions.explain: Chemical fishing introduces toxic poisons into the water that not only kill fish of all sizes indiscriminately but also leave harmful residues in the fish tissues, posing a deadly health risk to humans who consume them.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
